description: The extension handoff opens a Start decision before a browser transfer can begin.
Starting is an explicit user action rather than an automatic queue side effect.
The sender origin is carried into the visible Start surface.
A raw extension handoff is normalized and bound before it enters the queue.
Active transfer progress is a distinct surface.
Received bytes, total bytes, rate, and ETA are rendered from the job record.
The active surface exposes real pause and resume actions beside cancel.
The active surface exposes a real cancellation action.
Completion is a separate non-blocking notice.
The completion notice remains dismissible without hiding the record.
The active queue id selects exactly one surface state.
Requested, active, unsupported, and unknown presentation outcomes stay distinct.
The installed extension opens its own Start surface before a browser transfer.
The service worker trusts the browser-supplied extension id and origin only.
The worker prepares an in-memory proposal without starting a browser transfer.
Only explicit Start confirmation calls the browser download API.
Browser download events drive progress and terminal outcomes.
The active transfer pause action reaches the browser API.
The active transfer resume action reaches the browser API.
The active transfer cancel action reaches the browser API.
Opening a completed file uses the browser download record.
Completion and interruption are reported through a non-blocking browser notification.
The worker queries the host result instead of accepting a self-reported window state.
The extension-owned page declares the Start surface as a real accessible dialog.
The Start button sends the explicit confirmation message.
The extension-owned page includes a separate active progress surface.
The extension-owned page includes a separate completion surface.
The extension window reads the real worker state instead of simulating progress.
Duplicate button actions are refused while a worker action is pending.
Completion notifications are explicitly declared by the extension manifest.
Pending actions are visibly disabled while their worker request settles.
Start and active surfaces share Escape, focus-trap, and disposal behavior.
When Start disappears, focus moves to an available action without completion autofocus.
Retry re-arms exactly one worker-state polling loop.
React active surfaces refuse duplicate pause, resume, cancel, retry, or dismiss actions.
React completion Open reports pending and failure state.
React completion visibly reports the always-on-top outcome.
The dialog focus route has an executable hidden-Start regression test.
An unknown active id renders a recoverable error instead of disappearing.
